newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG Metals denies futures losses, stock plunges.
newsitem.headline: LG Metals denies futures losses, stock plunges.

text.p: South Korea's largest metals producer, LG Metals Corp, on Thursday denied any losses from futures trading after its share price plunged on rumours it was in trouble on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
"No losses have been made from metals futures trading," the company said in a statement.
LG metals said it had recorded a 39.4 billion won ($46 million) profit from metals futures trading last year.
But the statement did not say whether LG Metals had any current open positions in international metal markets.

Earlier rumours that LG Metals was in trouble on the LME as a result of incorrectly betting that base metal markets such as copper, aluminium and zinc would fall, had sent its share price tumbling by eight percent.
The statement failed to lift the stock's price, and LG closed 1,200 won lower at 13,800 won, its floor for the day.
Yoo Nam-gil, an analyst with Hyundai Securties, said rumours were flying that LG was in difficulties on the LME.
"LG Metals is expected to face further selling pressure," Yoo said.
South Korean investors are currently particularly sensitive to such rumours when the local financial markets are being battered by the scandal surrounding the domestic conglomerate, the Hanbo Group.

Some traders in London said they believed LG Metals had been caught in a "short" position on the copper market by a European merchant going "long". The merchant was trying to push up prices by squeezing physical supplies, they said.
Speculation over LG Metals has unsettled the LME, rocked last year by a scandal over Japan's Sumitomo.

The Japanese trading house last June fired its former chief copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he had admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading. largest producer of copper, gold and silver.
The statement said the company had been actively hedging against risks from changes in non-ferrous metals prices.

On Wednesday, the LG Metals official in charge of LME trading said the firm had not requested increased credit lines from the exchange or received margin calls from brokers, which would force it to put up more collateral to cover its open
positions.
Hong Seong-ho said LG took a short position on copper to hedge physical stocks carried forward from last year.
Some metals traders have said LME chief executive David King sent a letter to LG expressing concen about the company's operations. But Hong said he had no knowledge of any letter.
King declined to comment on the issue on Wednesday.
Most South Korean futures brokers dismiss LME rumours that LG Metals has a short position of 100,000-200,000 tonnes of copper.
An analyst with the Daewoo Economic Research Institute estimated LG Metals' sales in 1995 totalled 1.384 trillion won.
The company's ordinary profit in 1995 was 48.4 billion won ($56 million), which included 12 billion won ($14 million) profit from its futures trade.
At least three LG companies trade LME futures, including LG Metals, LG Cable and Machinary Ltd, and LG International Corp, Korean traders said.

Domestic base metals demand, already dampened by nationwide strikes and a financial crisis at the country's 14th largest industrial conglomerate, the Hanbo Group, was frozen this week on the LG rumours, metal traders said.
